text:
nora: quick note: I hit an onboarding footgun with the Go generator stream today. When we trigger an auth refresh mid-stream the SDK sometimes leaves a reader goroutine alive after ctx cancel. Repro in sampleapp/generator/renewal-repro.go. Anyone have bandwidth to look?

ash: saw that pattern before. The root cause in my patch was double-close semantics: the internal socket reader and the user-facing Close() both try to close the same done channel which can leave a goroutine blocked on a send.

raul: Can you sketch how you're wiring ctx vs the internal lifecycle? In our Go consumers we tend to conflate context cancellation and stream Abort which makes it hard to reason about retries.

nora: minimal sketch below. user cancels context on SIGINT; auth refresh sends an error event and we surface that to the caller.

```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(parentCtx)
stream, err := client.Generator.Stream(ctx, req)
if err != nil { return err }

go func() {
  for stream.Next() {
    ev := stream.Event()
    handle(ev)
  }
  if err := stream.Err(); err != nil {
    log.Printf("stream finished: %v", err)
  }
}()

// later on signal
cancel()
```

kevin: two suggestions: 1) separate "user intent" (Abort) from "transport lifecycle" (Close). Relying solely on ctx.Done() mixes concerns. 2) give the stream a small finite state machine internally and avoid broadcasting raw channel closes to both internal reader and external waiter.

ash: SDK parity note: Node exposes stream.abort() and stream.resume(token). Python returns a ResumeToken in the AuthExpired exception. Go lacking an explicit Abort/Resume makes the UX surprising. Apps expect resume semantics for long-lived sessions.

raul: We should avoid implicit resume for now. If we return a resume token in the AuthExpired event, the app can call Resume(token) explicitly; that keeps semantics clear and avoids hidden reconnects that duplicate output. But we need APIs for deduping if the resumed connection replays the final chunk. Two ideas: sequence IDs per event or opaque resume markers the service can use to trim.

nora: I like explicit Resume + Abort. Proposal for Go API: type GeneratorStream interface { Next() bool; Event() *Event; Err() error; Abort(); Resume(token string) error; Close() error } Also add Event.SequenceID string in the response so apps can de-dup. Docs should say Resume is optional and may replay last N events.

kevin: implementation note: make Abort() set an atomic flag and cancel an internal context, but do not call user ctx.Cancel(). That preserves user's control while stopping internal goroutines. Also avoid closing shared channels more than once.

ash: CI found a flake: generator_resume_race_test failing intermittently on main. I filed https://ci/internal/issue/6789 and temporarily pinned the test to flaky.

ci-bot: :robot_face: nightly: generator_resume_race_test failed 2/10. See logs: https://ci/internal/6789/log.

nora: action items: kevin -> sketch internal FSM + PR to add Abort() semantics; ash -> add resume_token field in AuthExpired events and sequenceID on events; raul -> update sampleapp/generator to show Abort vs Cancel pattern and de-dup example; I'll write a tiny unit test that deterministically races auth refresh+cancel so CI can validate the fix.

kevin: I'll also add a short note in the Go SDK README under "Streaming gotchas" describing difference between ctx cancel and Abort(). That should reduce onboarding pain.

nora: thanks all. small follow-up: can we sync with node/python owners to align resume_token shape so customers can port logic easily? scheduling a 15m sync tomorrow. :thumbsup:
